The main takeaway from our work is that
the superfluid-normal fluid interaction is strong and can be used to explain the observed properties of neutron stars.

the superfluid-normal fluid coupling is strong enough for the neutron star to break up into alternating domains of proton superconductors and normal fluids, which in turn leads to a strong dissipation.
the superconducting cores are not a single-phase medium, as usually assumed, but rather are a complex mixture of superconducting, normal fluid, and superfluid phases.
